Since proxied contracts do not make use of a constructor, it's common to move constructor logic to an external initializer function, usually called `initialize`. It then becomes necessary to protect this initializer function so it can only be called once. The {initializer} modifier provided by this contract will have this effect. The initialization functions use a version number. Once a version number is used, it is consumed and cannot be reused. This mechanism prevents re-execution of each \"step\" but allows the creation of new initialization steps in case an upgrade adds a module that needs to be initialized. For example: [.hljs-theme-light.nopadding] ```solidity contract MyToken is ERC20Upgradeable {     function initialize() initializer public {         __ERC20_init(\"MyToken\", \"MTK\");     } } contract MyTokenV2 is MyToken, ERC20PermitUpgradeable {     function initializeV2() reinitializer(2) public {         __ERC20Permit_init(\"MyToken\");     } } ``` TIP: To avoid leaving the proxy in an uninitialized state, the initializer function should be called as early as possible by providing the encoded function call as the `_data` argument to {ERC1967Proxy-constructor}. CAUTION: When used with inheritance, manual care must be taken to not invoke a parent initializer twice, or to ensure that all initializers are idempotent. This is not verified automatically as constructors are by Solidity. [CAUTION] ==== Avoid leaving a contract uninitialized. An uninitialized contract can be taken over by an attacker. This applies to both a proxy and its implementation contract, which may impact the proxy. To prevent the implementation contract from being used, you should invoke the {_disableInitializers} function in the constructor to automatically lock it when it is deployed: [.hljs-theme-light.nopadding] ```","errors":{"InvalidInitialization()":[{"details":"The contract is already initialized."}],"NotInitializing()":[{"details":"The contract is not initializing."}]},"events":{"Initialized(uint64)":{"details":"Triggered when the contract has been initialized or reinitialized."}},"kind":"dev","methods":{},"version":1},"userdoc":{"kind":"user","methods":{},"version":1}},"settings":{"compilationTarget":{"lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol":"Initializable"},"evmVersion":"cancun","libraries":{},"metadata":{"bytecodeHash":"ipfs"},"optimizer":{"enabled":true,"runs":200},"remappings":[":@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable/contracts/",":@openzeppelin/contracts/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/",":forge-std/=lib/forge-std/src/",":openzeppelin-foundry-upgrades/=lib/openzeppelin-foundry-upgrades/src/"]},"sources":{"lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol":{"keccak256":"0xdb4d24ee2c087c391d587cd17adfe5b3f9d93b3110b1388c2ab6c7c0ad1dcd05","license":"MIT","urls":["bzz-raw://ab7b6d5b9e2b88176312967fe0f0e78f3d9a1422fa5e4b64e2440c35869b5d08","dweb:/ipfs/QmXKYWWyzcLg1B2k7Sb1qkEXgLCYfXecR9wYW5obRzWP1Q"]}},"version":1}

StorageSlot.metadata: {"compiler":{"version":"0.8.38+commit.1835d247"},"language":"Solidity","output":{"abi":[],"devdoc":{"details":"Library for reading and writing primitive types to specific storage slots. Storage slots are often used to avoid storage conflict when dealing with upgradeable contracts. This library helps with reading and writing to such slots without the need for inline assembly. The functions in this library return Slot structs that contain a `value` member that can be used to read or write. Example usage to set ERC-1967 implementation slot: ```solidity contract ERC1967 {     // Define the slot. Alternatively, use the SlotDerivation library to derive the slot.     bytes32 internal constant _IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT = 0x360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbc;     function _getImplementation() internal view returns (address) {         return StorageSlot.getAddressSlot(_IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT).value;     }     function _setImplementation(address newImplementation) internal {         require(newImplementation.code.length > 0);         StorageSlot.getAddressSlot(_IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT).value = newImplementation;     } } ``` TIP: Consider using this library along with {SlotDerivation}.","kind":"dev","methods":{},"version":1},"userdoc":{"kind":"user","methods":{},"version":1}},"settings":{"compilationTarget":{"lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/utils/StorageSlot.sol":"StorageSlot"},"evmVersion":"cancun","libraries":{},"metadata":{"bytecodeHash":"ipfs"},"optimizer":{"enabled":true,"runs":200},"remappings":[":@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable/contracts/",":@openzeppelin/contracts/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/",":forge-std/=lib/forge-std/src/",":openzeppelin-foundry-upgrades/=lib/openzeppelin-foundry-upgrades/src/"]},"sources":{"lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/utils/StorageSlot.sol":{"keccak256":"0xcf74f855663ce2ae00ed8352666b7935f6cddea2932fdf2c3ecd30a9b1cd0e97","license":"MIT","urls":["bzz-raw://9f660b1f351b757dfe01438e59888f31f33ded3afcf5cb5b0d9bf9aa6f320a8b","dweb:/ipfs/QmarDJ5hZEgBtCmmrVzEZWjub9769eD686jmzb2XpSU1cM"]}},"version":1}

These should be exposed in the external API and be unique. The best way to achieve this is by using `public constant` hash digests: ```solidity bytes32 public constant MY_ROLE = keccak256(\"MY_ROLE\"); ``` Roles can be used to represent a set of permissions. Each role has an associated admin role, and only accounts that have a role's admin role can call {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. By default, the admin role for all roles is `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which means that only accounts with this role will be able to grant or revoke other roles. More complex role relationships can be created by using {_setRoleAdmin}. WARNING: The `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is also its own admin: it has permission to grant and revoke this role. IManicFlashOptionSettlement.metadata: {"compiler":{"version":"0.8.38+commit.1835d247"},"language":"Solidity","output":{"abi":[{"inputs":[{"internalType":"bytes32","name":"marketId","type":"bytes32"},{"internalType":"uint16","name":"leverage","type":"uint16"},{"internalType":"int64","name":"price","type":"int64"},{"internalType":"uint48","name":"publishTime","type":"uint48"},{"internalType":"bytes32[]","name":"ids","type":"bytes32[]"}],"name":"liquidate","outputs":[{"internalType":"uint256","name":"processed","type":"uint256"}],"stateMutability":"nonpayable","type":"function"},{"inputs":[{"internalType":"bytes32[]","name":"ids","type":"bytes32[]"}],"name":"refundExpired","outputs":[{"internalType":"uint256","name":"processed","type":"uint256"}],"stateMutability":"nonpayable","type":"function"},{"inputs":[{"internalType":"uint256","name":"maxCount","type":"uint256"}],"name":"repay","outputs":[{"internalType":"uint256","name":"repaid","type":"uint256"}],"stateMutability":"nonpayable","type":"function"},{"inputs":[{"internalType":"bytes32","name":"marketId","type":"bytes32"},{"internalType":"uint16","name":"leverage","type":"uint16"},{"internalType":"int64","name":"price","type":"int64"},{"internalType":"uint48","name":"publishTime","type":"uint48"},{"internalType":"bytes32[]","name":"ids","type":"bytes32[]"}],"name":"settle","outputs":[{"internalType":"uint256","name":"processed","type":"uint256"}],"stateMutability":"nonpayable","type":"function"}],"devdoc":{"author":"Manic","custom:security-contact":"See SECURITY.md","details":"The settler is trusted for the price only: each position's own times and line are      checked against the tick. `liquidate`, `settle` and `repay` work while a market is paused or switched off,      and while the circuit breaker is tripped; only the halt stops them (\u00a78.10), so a bet can always end once the      operator releases the halt. No brake stops `refundExpired`, which only ever returns a user's own stake.      A batch skips any position that has already ended, with {PositionSkipped}: sold, liquidated, settled or      refunded earlier, or listed twice in the same batch. An id that was never opened, or a position of another      market, still reverts the whole batch, with the id in the error, so the backend can drop it and resend.      Free money is measured position by position, in batch order: an earlier position's released stake or loss      counts for the next one's loser fee and payout. Fees accrue in the pool's pending fees      once per batch; anyone sweeps them to the fee recipient later (`sweepFees`). `liquidate`, `settle` and      `repay` also count their users' winnings and losses in the payout circuit breaker once per call (\u00a78.11);      a refund counts nothing.","kind":"dev","methods":{"liquidate(bytes32,uint16,int64,uint48,bytes32[])":{"details":"For each position, in order: free money is measured with its stake still held, the stake and its max      profit are released, the loser fee leaves the pool's total, and the position closes (slot 0 stays as the      tombstone, slot 1 is cleared). Emits {PositionLiquidated} per position ended and {PositionSkipped} per      position that had already ended. After the loop, the batch's fees are added to the pending fees and to      `feesPaid`, and its liquidated stakes are counted as losses in the payout circuit breaker (\u00a78.11). No      tokens move. Old ticks are accepted, so the backend can catch up after an outage. Requirements (in check order): - The caller holds `SETTLER_ROLE` (`AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount`). - The contract is not halted (`Halted`). - `ids` has 1 to 100 ids (`EmptyBatch` / `BatchSizeTooLarge`). - The market exists at this feed and leverage (`UnknownMarket`). - For each id, in order: it was opened (`UnknownPosition(id)`) on this market, so at this leverage   (`ConfigMismatch(id)`); if it is still open, then the price is positive (`InvalidPrice`), the tick is inside   the position's life, both ends included (`InvalidLiquidationWindow(id)`), and at most the market's clock skew   ahead of the chain's clock (`PriceFromFuture`), and the price touches the line, equality included   (`LiquidationPriceNotReached(id)`). - The pool's books stay within their types (`MathOverflow`).","params":{"ids":"The positions to liquidate.","leverage":"The market's leverage; every position in `ids` must have been opened at it.","marketId":"The market's Pyth feed id; every position in `ids` must belong to it.","price":"The tick's price, at the market's exponent.","publishTime":"The tick's publish time."},"returns":{"processed":"The number of positions liquidated; skipped ids are not counted."}},"refundExpired(bytes32[])":{"details":"For each position, in order: its stake and max profit are released, the stake leaves the pool's total, and      the position closes (slot 0 stays as the tombstone, slot 1 is cleared). Then {PositionRefunded} is      emitted, and the whole stake is paid back through `_pay`: no fee is taken, and if the token refuses the      transfer (a frozen user, a paused token), it waits in the user's claimable balance ({PayoutDeferred}),      and the rest of the batch goes on. Free money doesn't change: the stake was held for the position and      leaves with it, so the payout circuit breaker counts nothing. Emits {PositionSkipped} per position that      had already ended.      The delay is read when the refund runs, so a change by `setRefundDelay` applies to positions already      open. Once the delay has passed, `settle` and `liquidate` can still end a position too; whichever lands      first ends it, and the other skips it. The backend settles within seconds of expiry, so this only      matters after an outage of at least the delay (24 hours by default). LeverageMath.metadata: {"compiler":{"version":"0.8.38+commit.1835d247"},"language":"Solidity","output":{"abi":[],"devdoc":{"author":"Manic","custom:security-contact":"See SECURITY.md","details":"Units:      - prices: `int64` at the market's price exponent (BTC: -8, so $83,884 is 8_388_400_000_000);      - amounts: `uint64` base units of the token (USDG has 6 decimals, so $10 is 10_000_000);      - the leverage L: a whole number from 1 to 10,000 (1000 is 1000x);      - payout multiples (g, floor, cap) and fee rates: basis points, where 10_000 is 1x or 100%;      - the liquidation distance \u03b8: `thetaE7 = \u03b8 \u00d7 1e7`, so 2.627 bp is 2_627. documentation.text: @dev The `account` is missing a role.

@dev The caller of a function is not the expected one.
 NOTE: Don't confuse with {AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount}.

@dev Emitted when `account` is revoked `role`.
 `sender` is the account that originated the contract call:
   - if using `revokeRole`, it is the admin role bearer
   - if using `renounceRole`, it is the role bearer (i.e. `account`)
@dev Returns `true` if `account` has been granted `role`.

@dev Revokes `role` from `account`.
 If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event.
 Requirements:
 - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role.

@dev Revokes `role` from the calling account.
 Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's
 purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges
 if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced).
 If the calling account had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked}
 event.
 Requirements:
 - the caller must be `callerConfirmation`.
@dev External interface of AccessControl declared to support ERC-165 detection.
@dev The new default admin is not a valid default admin.

@dev At least one of the following rules was violated:
 - The `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` must only be managed by itself.
 - The `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` must only be held by one account at the time.
 - Any `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` transfer must be in two delayed steps.
@dev Emitted when a {pendingDefaultAdmin} is reset if it was never accepted, regardless of its schedule.

@dev Emitted when a {defaultAdminDelay} change is started, setting `newDelay` as the next

@dev Initiates a {defaultAdminDelay} update by setting a {pendingDefaultAdminDelay} scheduled for getting
 into effect after the current timestamp plus a {defaultAdminDelay}.
 This function guarantees that any call to {beginDefaultAdminTransfer} done between the timestamp this
 method is called and the {pendingDefaultAdminDelay} effect schedule will use the current {defaultAdminDelay}
 set before calling.
 The {pendingDefaultAdminDelay}'s effect schedule is defined in a way that waiting until the schedule and then
 calling {beginDefaultAdminTransfer} with the new delay will take at least the same as another {defaultAdmin}
 complete transfer (including acceptance).
 The schedule is designed for two scenarios:
 - When the delay is changed for a larger one the schedule is `block.timestamp + newDelay` capped by
 {defaultAdminDelayIncreaseWait}.
 - When the delay is changed for a shorter one, the schedule is `block.timestamp + (current delay - new delay)`.
 A {pendingDefaultAdminDelay} that never got into effect will be canceled in favor of a new scheduled change.
 Requirements:
 - Only can be called by the current {defaultAdmin}.
 Emits a {DefaultAdminDelayChangeScheduled} event and may emit a {DefaultAdminDelayChangeCanceled} event.

documentation.text:
@dev A modifier that defines a protected reinitializer function that can be invoked at most once, and only if the
 contract hasn't been initialized to a greater version before. In its scope, `onlyInitializing` functions can be
 used to initialize parent contracts.
 A reinitializer may be used after the original initialization step. This is essential to configure modules that
 are added through upgrades and that require initialization.
 When `version` is 1, this modifier is similar to `initializer`, except that functions marked with `reinitializer`
 cannot be nested. If one is invoked in the context of another, execution will revert.
 Note that versions can jump in increments greater than 1; this implies that if multiple reinitializers coexist in
 a contract, executing them in the right order is up to the developer or operator.
 WARNING: Setting the version to 2**64 - 1 will prevent any future reinitialization.
 Emits an {Initialized} event.

@dev Returns the address that signed a hashed message (`hash`) with `signature` or an error. This will not
 return address(0) without also returning an error description. Errors are documented using an enum (error type)
 and a bytes32 providing additional information about the error.
 If no error is returned, then the address can be used for verification purposes.
 The `ecrecover` EVM precompile allows for malleable (non-unique) signatures:
 this function rejects them by requiring the `s` value to be in the lower
 half order, and the `v` value to be either 27 or 28.
 NOTE: This function only supports 65-byte signatures. ERC-2098 short signatures are rejected. This restriction
 is DEPRECATED and will be removed in v6.0. Developers SHOULD NOT use signatures as unique identifiers; use hash
 invalidation or nonces for replay protection.
 IMPORTANT: `hash` _must_ be the result of a hash operation for the
 verification to be secure: it is possible to craft signatures that
 recover to arbitrary addresses for non-hashed data. A safe way to ensure
 this is by receiving a hash of the original message (which may otherwise
 be too long), and then calling {MessageHashUtils-toEthSignedMessageHash} on it.
 Documentation for signature generation:
 - with https://web3js.readthedocs.io/en/v1.3.4/web3-eth-accounts.html#sign[Web3.js]
 - with https://docs.ethers.io/v5/api/signer/#Signer-signMessage[ethers]

@dev Returns the EIP-712 domain separator constructed from an `eip712Domain`. See {IERC5267-eip712Domain}

@dev Verifies multiple ERC-7913 `signatures` for a given `hash` using a set of `signers`.
 Returns `false` if the number of signers and signatures is not the same.
 The signers should be ordered by their `keccak256` hash to ensure efficient duplication check. Unordered
 signers are supported, but the uniqueness check will be more expensive.
 NOTE: Unlike ECDSA signatures, contract signatures are revocable, and the outcome of this function can thus
 change through time. It could return true at block N and false at block N+1 (or the opposite).

@dev Calculate the modular multiplicative inverse of a number in Z/nZ.
 If n is a prime, then Z/nZ is a field. In that case all elements are inversible, except 0.
 If n is not a prime, then Z/nZ is not a field, and some elements might not be inversible.
 If the input value is not inversible, 0 is returned.
 NOTE: If you know for sure that n is (big) a prime, it may be cheaper to use Fermat's little theorem and get the
 inverse using `Math.modExp(a, n - 2, n)`. See {invModPrime}.

@dev Variant of {invMod}. More efficient, but only works if `p` is known to be a prime greater than `2`.
 From https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat%27s_little_theorem[Fermat's little theorem], we know that if p is
 prime, then `a**(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p`. As a consequence, we have `a * a**(p-2) ≡ 1 mod p`, which means that
 `a**(p-2)` is the modular multiplicative inverse of a in Fp.
 NOTE: this function does NOT check that `p` is a prime greater than `2`.

@dev Returns the modular exponentiation of the specified base, exponent and modulus (b ** e % m)
 Requirements:
 - modulus can't be zero
 - underlying staticcall to precompile must succeed
 IMPORTANT: The result is only valid if the underlying call succeeds. When using this function, make
 sure the chain you're using it on supports the precompiled contract for modular exponentiation
 at address 0x05 as specified in https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-198[EIP-198]. Otherwise,
 the underlying function will succeed given the lack of a revert, but the result may be incorrectly
 interpreted as 0.

@dev Contract module that allows children to implement role-based access
 control mechanisms. This is a lightweight version that doesn't allow enumerating role
 members except through off-chain means by accessing the contract event logs. Some
 applications may benefit from on-chain enumerability, for those cases see
 {AccessControlEnumerable}.
 Roles are referred to by their `bytes32` identifier. These should be exposed
 in the external API and be unique. The best way to achieve this is by
 using `public constant` hash digests:
 ```solidity
 bytes32 public constant MY_ROLE = keccak256("MY_ROLE");
 ```
 Roles can be used to represent a set of permissions. To restrict access to a
 function call, use {hasRole}:
 ```solidity
 function foo() public {
     require(hasRole(MY_ROLE, msg.sender));
     ...
 }
 ```
 Roles can be granted and revoked dynamically via the {grantRole} and
 {revokeRole} functions. Each role has an associated admin role, and only
 accounts that have a role's admin role can call {grantRole} and {revokeRole}.
 By default, the admin role for all roles is `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which means
 that only accounts with this role will be able to grant or revoke other
 roles. More complex role relationships can be created by using
 {_setRoleAdmin}.
 WARNING: The `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is also its own admin: it has permission to
 grant and revoke this role. Extra precautions should be taken to secure
 accounts that have been granted it. We recommend using {AccessControlDefaultAdminRules}
 to enforce additional security measures for this role.

@dev Extension of {AccessControl} that allows specifying special rules to manage
 the `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` holder, which is a sensitive role with special permissions
 over other roles that may potentially have privileged rights in the system.
 If a specific role doesn't have an admin role assigned, the holder of the
 `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` will have the ability to grant it and revoke it.
 This contract implements the following risk mitigations on top of {AccessControl}:
 * Only one account holds the `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` since deployment until it's potentially renounced.
 * Enforces a 2-step process to transfer the `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` to another account.
 * Enforces a configurable delay between the two steps, with the ability to cancel before the transfer is accepted.
 * The delay can be changed by scheduling, see {changeDefaultAdminDelay}.
 * Role transfers must wait at least one block after scheduling before it can be accepted.
 * It is not possible to use another role to manage the `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`.
 Example usage:
 ```solidity
 contract MyToken is AccessControlDefaultAdminRules {
   constructor() AccessControlDefaultAdminRules(
     3 days,
     msg.sender // Explicit initial `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` holder
    ) {}
 }
 ```

@dev https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712[EIP-712] is a standard for hashing and signing of typed structured data.
 The encoding scheme specified in the EIP requires a domain separator and a hash of the typed structured data, whose
 encoding is very generic and therefore its implementation in Solidity is not feasible, thus this contract
 does not implement the encoding itself. Protocols need to implement the type-specific encoding they need in order to
 produce the hash of their typed data using a combination of `abi.encode` and `keccak256`.
 This contract implements the EIP-712 domain separator ({_domainSeparatorV4}) that is used as part of the encoding
 scheme, and the final step of the encoding to obtain the message digest that is then signed via ECDSA
 ({_hashTypedDataV4}).
 The implementation of the domain separator was designed to be as efficient as possible while still properly updating
 the chain id to protect against replay attacks on an eventual fork of the chain.
 NOTE: This contract implements the version of the encoding known as "v4", as implemented by the JSON RPC method
 https://docs.metamask.io/guide/signing-data.html[`eth_signTypedDataV4` in MetaMask].
 NOTE: The upgradeable version of this contract does not use an immutable cache and recomputes the domain separator
 each time {_domainSeparatorV4} is called. This is cheaper than accessing a cached version in cold storage.

@notice Settles every position in `ids` that expires at the tick's second, at the tick's price: each pays
         `stake × g`, with the floor and the cap applied, less the 2% winner fee on the profit paid now, or the
         3% loser fee on a loss while free money is at or above the floor. Profit the pool can't pay now becomes
         an IOU at the back of the repay queue.
 @dev For each position, in order: g and the payout at the tick's price, at the market's leverage; the split with
      free money measured
      with its stake still held (while anyone is owed, a new winner's whole profit is queued, so nobody jumps
      the queue); the stake and its max profit released; what leaves the pool (the user's part and both fees)
      leaves its total. With nothing owed, the position closes (slot 0 stays as the tombstone, slot 1 is
      cleared). With profit owed, it becomes an IOU: the next queue number, the total owed, the IOU count and
      slot 2 are written, and slot 1 is kept. Then {PositionSettled} is emitted, and the user's part is paid
      through `_pay`: if the token refuses the transfer (a frozen user, a paused token), it waits in the user's
      claimable balance ({PayoutDeferred}), and the rest of the batch goes on. Emits {PositionSkipped} per
      position that had already ended. After the loop, the batch's fees are added to the pending fees and to
      `feesPaid`, and its profit paid now and its losses are counted in the payout circuit breaker, which may
      trip ({CircuitBreakerTripped}, after the batch's other events; §8.11). Old ticks are accepted, so the
      backend can catch up after an outage.
 Requirements (in check order):
 - The caller holds `SETTLER_ROLE` (`AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount`).
 - The contract is not halted (`Halted`).
 - `ids` has 1 to 100 ids (`EmptyBatch` / `BatchSizeTooLarge`).
 - The market exists at this feed and leverage (`UnknownMarket`).
 - The price is positive (`InvalidPrice`).
 - The tick is at most the market's clock skew ahead of the chain's clock, so the second has passed
   (`NotExpired`).
 - For each id, in order: it was opened (`UnknownPosition(id)`) on this market, so at this leverage
   (`ConfigMismatch(id)`); if it is still open, then it expires at exactly the tick's second
   (`InvalidPriceTimestamp(id)`), and the price doesn't touch its line (`LiquidateInstead(id)`: such a position
   is liquidated at the same tick).
 - The pool's books stay within their types (`MathOverflow`).
 - Each payout has at least 60,000 gas, and doesn't run out of gas (`InsufficientGasForPayout`).
 @param marketId The market's Pyth feed id; every position in `ids` must belong to it.
 @param leverage The market's leverage; every position in `ids` must have been opened at it.
 @param price The price at the close of the expiry second, at the market's exponent.
 @param publishTime The tick's publish time: the positions' expiry second.
 @param ids The positions to settle.
 @return processed The number of positions settled, IOUs included; skipped ids are not counted.

         stops it.
 @dev For each position, in order: its stake and max profit are released, the stake leaves the pool's total, and
      the position closes (slot 0 stays as the tombstone, slot 1 is cleared). Then {PositionRefunded} is
      emitted, and the whole stake is paid back through `_pay`: no fee is taken, and if the token refuses the
      transfer (a frozen user, a paused token), it waits in the user's claimable balance ({PayoutDeferred}),
      and the rest of the batch goes on. Free money doesn't change: the stake was held for the position and
      leaves with it, so the payout circuit breaker counts nothing. Emits {PositionSkipped} per position that
      had already ended.
      The delay is read when the refund runs, so a change by `setRefundDelay` applies to positions already
      open. Once the delay has passed, `settle` and `liquidate` can still end a position too; whichever lands
      first ends it, and the other skips it. The backend settles within seconds of expiry, so this only
      matters after an outage of at least the delay (24 hours by default).
 Requirements (in check order):
 - The refund is switched on: its delay is not 0 (`RefundDisabled`).
 - `ids` has 1 to 100 ids (`EmptyBatch` / `BatchSizeTooLarge`).
 - For each id, in order: it was opened (`UnknownPosition(id)`), on any market; if it is still open, then at
   least the refund delay has passed since its expiry, `block.timestamp ≥ endTime + refundDelaySecs`
   (`RefundTooEarly(id)`).
 - The pool's books stay within their types (`MathOverflow`).
 - Each payout has at least 60,000 gas, and doesn't run out of gas (`InsufficientGasForPayout`).
 @param ids The positions to refund. They may belong to different markets.
 @return processed The number of positions refunded; skipped ids are not counted.

@notice Repays the IOU queue out of the pool's free money, strictly in queue order, from the head. Anyone may
         call it: the backend after each settle batch, or an owner waiting to be paid.
 @dev Each repayment pays the head as much as free money allows, less the 2% winner fee (`repaySplit`): the
      amount leaves the pool's total and its total owed, and the IOU's `owed` drops by it. Only free money
      repays, so the stakes of open bets are never touched.
      A head paid in full leaves the queue: the owed count drops, the head moves on to the next IOU, its queue
      entry is deleted, and the position closes (slot 0 stays as the tombstone; slots 1 and 2 are cleared). The
      first IOU that free money covers only in part keeps the rest owed and stays at the head, and the call
      stops there. The call also stops when free money runs out, when the queue is empty, and after `maxCount`
      repayments, so with an empty queue or no free money it changes nothing.
      Emits {OwedRepaid} per repayment, then pays the owner through `_pay`: if the token refuses the transfer
      (a frozen owner, a paused token), it waits in the owner's claimable balance ({PayoutDeferred}), and the
      rest of the queue is still paid. After the loop, the winner fees are added to the pending fees and to
      `feesPaid`, and the amounts repaid are counted as profit in the payout circuit breaker, which may trip
      ({CircuitBreakerTripped}; §8.11).
 Requirements (in check order):
 - The contract is not halted (`Halted`).
 - `maxCount` is 1 to 50 (`InvalidMaxCount`).
 - The pool's books stay within their types (`MathOverflow`).
 - Each payout has at least 60,000 gas, and doesn't run out of gas (`InsufficientGasForPayout`).
 @param maxCount The most IOUs to repay in this call.
 @return repaid The number of IOUs repaid: each was paid in full, except perhaps the last, which may have been
         paid in part and is then the new head.

@title IManicFlashOptionSettlement
 @author Manic
 @notice How positions end at a price, how a position the backend never ended is refunded, and how the winners the
         pool couldn't pay are paid later. The settler relayer liquidates positions when a tick touches their line
         and settles them at their expiry second, in batches of up to 100 positions of one market (one feed at one
         leverage) at one price tick (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8.4, §8.5). Anyone refunds the stake of a position
         still open long after its expiry (the safety refund, §8.6), and anyone repays the IOU queue from the
         pool's free money (§8.7). Implemented by `SettlementModule`.
 @dev The settler is trusted for the price only: each position's own times and line are
      checked against the tick. `liquidate`, `settle` and `repay` work while a market is paused or switched off,
      and while the circuit breaker is tripped; only the halt stops them (§8.10), so a bet can always end once the
      operator releases the halt. No brake stops `refundExpired`, which only ever returns a user's own stake.
      A batch skips any position that has already ended, with {PositionSkipped}: sold, liquidated, settled or
      refunded earlier, or listed twice in the same batch. An id that was never opened, or a position of another
      market, still reverts the whole batch, with the id in the error, so the backend can drop it and resend.
      Free money is measured position by position, in batch order: an earlier position's released stake or loss
      counts for the next one's loser fee and payout. Fees accrue in the pool's pending fees
      once per batch; anyone sweeps them to the fee recipient later (`sweepFees`). `liquidate`, `settle` and
      `repay` also count their users' winnings and losses in the payout circuit breaker once per call (§8.11);
      a refund counts nothing.
 @custom:security-contact See SECURITY.md

@notice Opens a position: the user's signed order, at the price the relayer saw.
 @dev Records the position (stake held, lines locked), adds the stake to the pool's total and its held margin and
      the position's max profit to the open max profit, emits {PositionOpened}, and only then pulls the stake
      with the user's EIP-3009 authorisation, `a`, whose nonce is the position id. A failed pull reverts all of
      it. The position's clock starts at the entry tick, not when the transaction lands.
 Requirements (in check order):
 - The caller holds `OPENER_ROLE` (`AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount`).
 - The contract is not halted (`Halted`).
 - The order has not expired: `block.timestamp` ≤ `o.deadline` (`OrderExpired`).
 - The market of the order's feed at the order's leverage exists (`UnknownMarket`), is enabled
   (`LeverageDisabled`) and is not paused (`LeveragePaused`), and the circuit breaker has not tripped
   (`BreakerTripped`).
 - `o.positionId` is not zero and was never used (`PositionIdUsed`).
 - `signature` is `o.user`'s signature of the order (`InvalidSignature`).
 - The terms fit the market: the stake (`InvalidAmount`); an enabled duration, θ inside its rule, the floor, and
   a cap of at least the floor (`InvalidLeverageParams`).
 - The entry tick is at most the market's maximum age old (`PriceTooOld`) and at most its clock skew ahead
   (`PriceFromFuture`).
 - The entry tick is at or after `o.notBefore`, so the user signed before the price was known
   (`PriceBeforeOrder`).
 - The entry price is positive and the lines fit (`InvalidPrice` / `InvalidLeverageParams`).
 - The open gate lets the bet in (`OpenBlockedTotalOwed` / `OpenBlockedExposure`).
 - The pool's books stay within their types (`MathOverflow`).
 - The token moves exactly `o.stake` from `o.user` (the token's own error, or `TransferAmountMismatch`). USDG
   names its own bad-signature error `InvalidSignature` too; this function checks the order's signature first.
 @param o The order, signed by the user before the price was known.
 @param signature `o.user`'s signature of `o` (EIP-712), 65 bytes from an EOA.
 @param t The terms the relayer adds at the tick: the entry price and time, θ, the floor and the cap.
 @param a The user's EIP-3009 authorisation for exactly `o.stake`, with `o.positionId` as its nonce.

@notice Sells a position before its expiry: the user's signed order, at the price and the amounts the relayer
         quotes.
 @dev The relayer quotes the valuation (what the position is worth at the tick) and the sale amount (the
      valuation less the early-sell fee); the contract bounds both with its own maths, and the user's
      `minAmount` bounds the sale amount from below. A sale is never partly paid: it goes through only while
      nobody is owed and the pool can pay the whole valuation now, so it can never jump the repay queue.
      The position closes: its stake and max profit are released, the valuation and the loser fee leave the
      pool's total, and the early-sell, winner and loser fees go into the pending fees. Then {PositionSold} is
      emitted, the sale amount against the stake is counted in the payout circuit breaker as a profit or a
      loss, which may trip it ({CircuitBreakerTripped}; §8.11), and the user is paid the sale amount less the
      winner fee through `_pay`: if the token refuses the transfer (a frozen user, a paused token), it waits in
      the user's claimable balance ({PayoutDeferred}). A sale closes its position, so its order can never be
      used again.
 Requirements (in check order):
 - The caller holds `OPENER_ROLE` (`AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount`).
 - The contract is not halted (`Halted`).
 - The order has not expired: `block.timestamp` ≤ `s.deadline` (`OrderExpired`).
 - The position exists (`UnknownPosition(id)`). Its market is enabled (`LeverageDisabled`) and not paused
   (`LeveragePaused`), and the circuit breaker has not tripped (`BreakerTripped`).
 - The position is open (`PositionNotOpen`).
 - `signature` is the position's user's signature of the order (`InvalidSignature`).
 - The tick is inside the sell window: at least the market's minimum delay after the start, and more than its
   cutoff before the end; and the sale lands before the end, `block.timestamp < endTime` (`SellWindowClosed`
   for either).
 - The tick is at most the market's maximum age old (`PriceTooOld`) and at most its clock skew ahead
   (`PriceFromFuture`).
 - The tick is at or after `s.notBefore`, so the user signed before the price was known (`PriceBeforeOrder`).
 - The price is positive (`InvalidPrice`) and doesn't touch the position's line (`LiquidateInstead(id)`).
 - The valuation is at most what the position pays at this price (`ValuationAboveCurrentPayout`); the sale
   amount at most the valuation (`SellAmountExceedsValuation`); the early-sell fee at most the market's cap
   (`SellFeeTooHigh`); the sale amount at least `s.minAmount` (`SellAmountBelowMin`); nobody is owed
   (`QueueNotEmpty`); and the valuation within free money plus the position's own stake (`SellNotPayable`).
 - The pool's books stay within their types (`MathOverflow`).
 - The payout has at least 60,000 gas, and doesn't run out of gas (`InsufficientGasForPayout`).
 @param s The order, signed by the position's user before the price was known.
 @param signature The position's user's signature of `s` (EIP-712), 65 bytes from an EOA.
 @param t The terms the relayer adds at the tick: the price and its time, the valuation and the sale amount.

@title SettlementModule
 @author Manic
 @notice How positions end at a price, how a position the backend never ended is refunded, and how the winners the
         pool couldn't pay are paid later: `liquidate` when a tick touches their line, and `settle` at their expiry
         second, each in batches the settler relayer sends (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8.4, §8.5); `refundExpired`,
         which anyone calls to return the stake of a position still open long after its expiry (§8.6); and
         `repay`, which anyone calls to pay the IOU queue from free money (§8.7).
 @dev `liquidate` and `settle` run the batch checks (`_checkBatch`), then walk the ids in order. Each id is looked
      up and checked against the batch's market (`_batchPosition`); an ended one is skipped. Each open one is ended
      by `_liquidateOne` or `_settleOne`, which do the books for that position, so free money is measured in batch
      order. The batch's fees are accrued once, after the loop, and its winnings and losses are
      counted in the payout circuit breaker once (`_countForBreaker`, §8.11). Settle pays each user from inside the
      loop through `_pay`, which never reverts on a refused transfer, so one frozen winner can't block a batch.
      `refundExpired` takes ids of any market (`_knownPosition`), and `_refundOne` returns each open one's stake
      the same way. `repay` walks the queue itself from its head, one IOU at a time (`_repayHead`), and stops at
      the first it can only pay in part, and counts what it repaid in the breaker. A refund counts nothing. The
      private functions are listed in solhint's order: state-changing, then view, then pure.
 @custom:security-contact See SECURITY.md
